works.title: It Looks Like You're Trying To Take Over The World
works.why: a fictional short story by the same author treating the scaling hypothesis's implications, offered as companion reading

works.title: Situational Awareness
works.why: cited as further reading on where AI capability trends may lead, related to the scaling hypothesis

works.title: AI 2027
works.why: cited alongside Situational Awareness as further reading on forecasts of future AI capability

works.title: Human-like Neural Nets by Catapulting
works.why: cited as further speculation on why scaling deep learning produces human-like behavior

works.title: Meta-Learning with Memory-Augmented Neural Networks
works.why: early demonstration of implicit meta-learning in neural networks, cited as background for GPT-3's emergent meta-learning

works.title: Wang et al 2018
works.why: cited as background work on implicit meta-learning emerging in trained networks

works.title: Botvinick et al 2019a
works.why: cited as background on meta-reinforcement learning, tied to Botvinick's quote about meta-learning being unavoidable

works.title: Clune 2019
works.why: cited as further reading on implicit meta-learning in neural networks

works.title: Jukebox
works.why: OpenAI's raw-audio music generation model cited as another recent demonstration of the benefits of scale

works.title: Hernandez & Brown 2020
works.why: used to estimate how training costs for a fixed performance level fall over time due to algorithmic efficiency gains

works.title: Behind Deep Blue
works.why: source clarifying the actual cost estimates of IBM's Deep Blue chess project, used to contextualize GPT-3's compute cost

works.title: LeCun 2019 remark on GPT and AGI
works.why: quoted skepticism ('the cake is a lie') about whether GPT-style models are part of the path to AGI, which the essay argues against

works.title: Banko & Brill 2001
works.why: early example of a 'scissor effect' where neural/data-hungry methods eventually overtake other approaches as data scales

works.title: Brants et al 2007
works.why: another example of large-scale data causing simple methods to overtake more complex ones, used to frame GPT-3's scaling

works.title: Koehn & Knowles 2017
works.why: cited as another example of scaling curves crossing where neural methods eventually dominate

works.title: Thompson et al 2020
works.why: criticized as a poorly controlled attempt to infer scaling laws from disparate papers, contrasted with the well-controlled scaling papers

works.title: AlphaGo Zero
works.why: used as the compute benchmark compared to GPT-3's training cost, and as an example of the 'just stack more layers' scaling approach

works.title: Chuan Li's compute cost estimate
works.why: source of an estimate of GPT-3's training hardware cost used in the essay's cost discussion

works.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
works.why: shows that cutting prediction error follows clean power-law curves as models, data and compute grow

works.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3 paper)
works.why: reports GPT-3's scaling results and few-shot meta-learning abilities that the whole essay is built around

works.title: Hendrycks et al 2020
works.why: cited for a chart of GPT-3 model size versus question-answering performance

works.title: Schrimpf et al 2020
works.why: shown as evidence that scaled language models increasingly match human brain activity patterns

works.title: Warstadt et al 2020
works.why: shown as evidence that models pick up more human-like linguistic biases as training data increases

works.title: Child 2020
works.why: shown as evidence that very deep VAEs can catch up to GANs in image generation quality when scaled

works.title: Vahdat & Kautz 2020
works.why: further evidence that deep VAEs scale to match GAN-quality image generation

works.title: Dojolonga et al 2020
works.why: shows transfer-learning representations keep improving with scale even after classification accuracy plateaus

works.title: BiT (Big Transfer)
works.why: example of a classifier CNN that transfers and develops human-like errors when scaled up

works.title: Hill et al 2019
works.why: cited among examples of agents trained at scale developing generalizable abilities

works.title: Chaplot et al 2017
works.why: cited among examples of scaled agent training producing generalization

works.title: Yu et al 2018
works.why: cited among examples of scaled agent training producing generalization

works.title: Lake 2019
works.why: cited among examples relevant to generalization emerging from scaled training

works.title: MetaMimic
works.why: example of imitation-learning reinforcement learning generalizing across hundreds of tasks when trained on a deep network

works.title: Dactyl
works.why: robot hand control system shown to develop implicit runtime meta-learning after training on millions of randomized environments

works.title: DD-PPO
works.why: example of a reinforcement learning system that outperforms classical robot planners after scaling by orders of magnitude

works.title: Procgen / CoinRun
works.why: shows that training on enough procedurally generated game levels makes agents generalize to unseen levels, unlike training on only hundreds

works.title: StyleGAN
works.why: example of disentangled latent representations emerging with sufficiently deep embeddings, part of the blessings-of-scale evidence

works.title: GQN (Generative Query Network)
works.why: example cited where enough samples force factorized, disentangled representations to emerge

works.title: BigGAN
works.why: example of a GAN that stabilizes and benefits from unusually large minibatches at scale, like other blessings-of-scale cases

works.title: ViLBERT / VideoBERT
works.why: examples of multimodal learning producing better representations from fewer data, motivating interest in big multimodal models

works.title: AlphaZero
works.why: demonstrated superhuman Go play from scaled self-play training without the 'delusions' of earlier search-based systems

works.title: MuZero
works.why: shown that training an RNN end-to-end to predict reward on enough data can obsolete AlphaZero by learning tree search implicitly

works.title: AlphaStar
works.why: reached human-level StarCraft play using hundreds of competing self-play agents to cover possible strategies

works.title: iGPT / Vision Transformer
works.why: shown that scaling unsupervised image models without supervision can match the best specialized alternatives, paralleling GPT

works.title: GPT-f
works.why: mentioned as another case showing scaling's benefits to some degree, alongside iGPT and Vision Transformer

works.title: Orseau et al 2020
works.why: cited for the idea that big models encode countless small sub-models interpolating over the data

works.title: Viering & Loog 2021
works.why: cited regarding phase transitions in learning, relevant to how a model abruptly shifts from memorizing to generalizing

works.title: The Brain as a Universal Learning Machine
works.why: cited for the idea that the brain, like scalable neural network architectures, applies similar learning rules fairly uniformly

works.title: Hawkins (on cortical uniformity)
works.why: cited alongside the universal learning machine idea for the view that the brain applies one algorithm fairly uniformly

works.title: Envisioned evolution of NLP research through three eras
works.why: source of the figure depicting hypothetical S-curves of progress in natural language processing research

works.title: Natural Language Processing (Almost) from Scratch
works.why: quoted on whether the small entropy gap between n-gram models and humans could be closed by learning grammar and world knowledge

works.title: The Limits of Automatic Speech Recognition / n-gram entropy study
works.why: provides a measured per-character entropy of English using n-gram models, used as a comparison point for GPT-3's own loss

works.title: Prediction and Entropy of Printed English
works.why: classic estimate of the per-character entropy of English from human guessing experiments, used as a human benchmark for loss

works.title: The Quiet Enemy (in The Legacy of Hiroshima)
works.why: source of the Edward Teller anecdote about Bohr doubting an atomic bomb could be built, used as an analogy for skepticism about scaling

works.title: The Human Use of Human Beings
works.why: quoted on how publicly announcing that a hard problem (like the atomic bomb) is solvable accelerates its solution, paralleling AI scaling

works.title: Ilya Sutskever on scaling and conviction
works.why: quoted explaining that what was missing before scaling worked was conviction that existing methods plus scale would succeed

works.title: Zaremba interview on OpenAI Five
works.why: quoted describing how existing reinforcement learning methods, simply scaled up, worked surprisingly well on Dota 2

works.title: GShard
works.why: example of a mixture-of-experts model Google Brain pursued mainly for deployment in Google Translate rather than scaling for its own sake

works.title: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically
works.why: an early scaling-law paper showing predictable gains from data and model size, cited as evidence scaling research predates GPT-3

works.title: DynamicEmbedding
works.why: example of a very large embedding approach contrasted with genuinely 'dense' scaled models like GPT-3

works.title: Moravec's forecast of AI hardware progress (1998)
works.why: source of the decades-old prediction that affordable compute for human-level AI would arrive around the 2020s, central to the scaling hypothesis argument

works.title: Peter Norvig / Lukas Biewald interview
works.why: anecdote illustrating that lack of compute, not ideas, held back 1980s neural network research

works.title: Jeff Dean on computing slowdown
works.why: quoted noting the coincidence of machine learning's compute needs rising just as CPU performance growth slowed

works.title: Jim Gray 1999 remarks on AI and supercomputers
works.why: quoted making a since-refuted argument that having enough compute should already have produced machine intelligence

works.title: Greg Brockman on OA5 training
works.why: quoted describing how OpenAI Five kept improving with scale and never hit a wall

works.title: SayCan
works.why: example of a language model used to plan and execute real-world robot actions, cited as evidence tool AIs become agent AIs

works.title: The intentional stance
works.why: framework invoked to argue that modeling non-agentic systems as agents is a useful, broadly applicable trick that a neural net might also learn

works.title: An Introduction to Wittgenstein's Tractatus
works.why: source of the Wittgenstein anecdote used as an analogy for how a correct but counterintuitive framing (agency, heliocentrism) can feel false

works.title: Story Of Your Life
works.why: fiction cited to illustrate the variational, 'wanting to minimize a global quantity' way of describing physical processes
